items.title: 165,000 New Jobs: Does the Decline Narrative Fit?
items.body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reports October payroll employment rose by 165,000 and unemployment remained at 4.1%. These numbers do not mean every worker is thriving, but they complicate a simple economic-collapse narrative. The Galt question: can productive capacity grow while some individuals still lose bargaining power?
items.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Nov 6, 2026

items.title: The Job Openings Test: Freedom to Walk Away
items.body: September's JOLTS survey reported 7.5 million job openings, 5.4 million hires and 3.4 million quits. A market can look healthy in aggregate while individual workers feel trapped. The Galt question: how much freedom is practical when changing jobs carries substantial personal risk?
items.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics · Nov 3, 2026

items.title: Productivity Versus Price Pressure
items.body: The Treasury reports strong 2026 private investment and third-quarter GDP growth, while households continue to face higher prices. This is a tension worth testing, not proof of collective decline. Who receives the gains from new tools, and how freely can people participate in creating them?

items.title: What Should Government Do About AI's Winners and Losers?
items.body: Post-election debate is turning toward affordability, employment, public debt and AI-led investment. Competing positions favor market freedom, social protections or regulation. The Galt question: when does intervention preserve genuine choice, and when does it suppress productive experimentation?
